title: gdrive-mounts org registry
description: Non-secret registry of Google Workspace orgs and their mounts. Owns every runtime default: the home-manager module reads `defaults` as its option defaults, so a knob changed here changes the mount.

defaults.description: Every key here is read by nix/lib/plan.nix settingsFrom. Adding a key that settingsFrom does not read is dead config.

stateDir.description: Runtime state root. Holds rclone-<org>.conf (0600), stage/<org>/, last-error.<org>-<mount>.

mountRoot.description: Parent of every mountpoint and of every link.

cacheRoot.description: VFS cache root. A path under /Volumes/ or /mnt/ is treated as an external volume: the mount waits for it, then fails loud. Never spills onto the boot disk.

nfsCacheHandleLimit.description: rclone nfsmount only. Never passed to `rclone mount`; the flag does not exist there.

ioTimeout.description: rclone --timeout (IO idle). Must stay well under the NFS client's patience: macOS marks a mount 'not responding' after vfs.generic.nfs.client.initialdowndelay seconds (5). rclone's own default is 5m, which is what wedged neo on 2026-08-19.

connectTimeout.description: rclone --contimeout (connect). Same reasoning as ioTimeout; rclone's default is 1m.

lowLevelRetries.description: rclone --low-level-retries. Multiplies ioTimeout into the worst-case stall, so it is part of the same budget: 5m x 10 is up to 50 minutes on one operation.

attrTimeout.description: rclone --attr-timeout. How long the kernel may trust cached attributes before asking again.

pollInterval.description: rclone --poll-interval for backend change notification. A long dirCacheTime makes polling mandatory, and the poll is itself backend traffic that can stall — keep it far below dirCacheTime but not aggressive.

logLevel.description: rclone --log-level. At the NOTICE default rclone logs neither low-level retries nor pacer backoff, which is why the 2026-08-19 wedge presented as 'no error ever logged'.

statsInterval.description: rclone --stats. "0" disables the periodic stats block; launchd never rotates a log, and the watchdog heartbeat already carries liveness.

nfsMountOptions.description: NFS *client* mount options, passed one per `rclone nfsmount --option`. nfsmount only: on Darwin rclone shells out to mount(8), which execs /sbin/mount_nfs, so these reach the kernel; on `rclone mount` the same flag means libfuse options instead. rclone hardcodes only port/mountport/tcp. `soft`+`intr` remove the `hard,nointr` bistability that makes a transient stall permanent and unprobeable; macOS `timeo` is in TENTHS of a second, so timeo=100 is 10s; `dumbtimer` stops the dynamic round-trip estimator deriving a microsecond timeout from a loopback RTT, which is what makes the default so brittle here. Verify a change landed with `nfsstat -m`, never by assuming.

remoteControl.description: Serve rclone's rc API on a unix socket inside stateDir (never a TCP port). Lets the watchdog capture core/stats and vfs/stats without touching the wedged mountpoint.

watchdogEnable.description: Run a health-probe sidecar per mount. Without it a mount that stops serving while every process stays alive is never restarted.

watchdogIntervalSec.description: Seconds between probes. Must be comfortably longer than the observed flap period of the NFS status flag, or a transient stall reads as a wedge.

watchdogProbeTimeoutSec.description: How long a bounded filesystem probe may take before it counts as a failure.

watchdogFailureThreshold.description: Consecutive failed probes before the watchdog acts. Never 1: the not-responding flag is observed to flap on a ~15s timescale and clear on its own.

watchdogRestartFloorSec.description: Minimum seconds between watchdog restarts of one mount. Held wedges are still recorded, so a floor hides nothing.

teamDriveId.description: Shared-drive id. Required when driveKind is `shared`; render-config.sh appends `team_drive` to the stanza from it.

mounts.description: One root mount per org. A second mount over the same drive doubles polling, VFS cache and dir-cache state; use `links` instead.

links.description: Symlinks into the org root mount, created at activation as <mountRoot>/<org>-<name> -> <root mountpoint>/<target>.

$comment: NON-SECRET registry. client_id, client_secret and token never appear here; they arrive at activation from operator-held files. Any token-shaped string in this file is a gitleaks event. Secret handling is owned by docs/sops-integration.md.
